title: Symlink-safe scanning and the agent rules layout
summary: This change does two things. In the scanner, `collect_files` and `resolve_scan_targets` now use `symlink_metadata` and refuse to follow symlinks: a link is counted as excluded rather than read as the file or directory it points at, so a link that cycles back on an ancestor can no longer recurse forever, and a scan of nothing but links is never reported clean. Alongside it, the repository's agent rules are reorganised: the root `AGENTS.md` is trimmed to cross-cutting rules and a routing table, folder-scoped rules move into `crates/AGENTS.md` and `.github/workflows/AGENTS.md`, seven new skills land under `.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills` becomes a git symlink to that folder, and CI gains a skill lint plus a check that the symlink is still a real symlink.

lanes.label: Invocation
lanes.subtitle: CLI and CI entry points
lanes.summary: Where a scan or a lint run is asked for: the `osf` binary on a developer's machine, and the CI jobs that call it.

lanes.label: osf engine
lanes.subtitle: crates/osf
lanes.summary: The library the binary calls into: target resolution, the file walk, and the rule engine that judges each file.

lanes.label: Filesystem
lanes.subtitle: working tree and git index
lanes.summary: What the scanner reads: git-tracked files, explicitly named paths, and the symlinks among them that are now counted rather than followed.

lanes.label: Agent rules
lanes.subtitle: AGENTS.md, skills, CI checks
lanes.summary: The documentation and skill surface every coding agent reads, plus the CI steps that keep it honest.

nodes.label: osf CLI
nodes.subtitle: osf scan / osf lint skill
nodes.summary: The thin command-line shell. It parses arguments, calls into the library, and prints the result; it holds no scanning logic of its own.

nodes.label: ci.yml
nodes.subtitle: hygiene job
nodes.summary: The pull request gate. This change adds two steps to it: one that lints every skill under `skills/` and `.agents/skills/`, and one that fails the build unless `.claude/skills` is recorded by git as a symlink pointing at `../.agents/skills`.

nodes.label: scan_paths
nodes.subtitle: pub fn scan_paths(dir, paths, rules, excluder)
nodes.summary: The scan entry point. It now takes the skipped-link count from target resolution as the starting value of `dropped`, and re-checks each resolved target with `symlink_metadata` before reading it, so a link that survived resolution is still counted as excluded rather than read.

nodes.label: resolve_scan_targets
nodes.subtitle: returns (targets, skipped)
nodes.summary: Turns the caller's paths into labelled files to read. With no paths it returns git's tracked files and a skipped count of zero; with paths it walks them and now returns how many symlinks were skipped instead of walked.

nodes.label: collect_files
nodes.subtitle: recursive walk, symlink-aware
nodes.summary: The recursive directory walk. It now calls `symlink_metadata` rather than `metadata`, and on seeing a symlink increments `skipped` and returns without descending. That single check is what makes a self-referential link terminate instead of recursing forever.

nodes.label: Rule engine
nodes.subtitle: Rules, Excluder, ScanOutcome
nodes.summary: The rules and excluder that decide what a file is judged against, and the outcome that carries the scanned files and the excluded count. Unchanged here, but the excluded count it reports now includes skipped symlinks.

nodes.label: git tracked files
nodes.subtitle: crate::git::tracked_files
nodes.summary: The default scan set: every file git tracks in the repository, labelled by its git-relative name. A tracked symlink appears here like any other entry, which is why the per-target symlink check in `scan_paths` matters.

nodes.label: Working tree
nodes.subtitle: files and directories on disk
nodes.summary: The real files and directories the scanner reads. Explicitly named paths are walked here, and this is where a symlink can point outside the scanned folder or back at an ancestor.

nodes.label: Symlinks
nodes.subtitle: counted, never followed
nodes.summary: Links found among the given paths or while walking them. They are no longer read as the file or directory they point at; each one increments the excluded count, so a scan that skipped everything still says so.

nodes.label: AGENTS.md
nodes.subtitle: root working context
nodes.summary: Trimmed to the rules every task needs, plus a routing table naming which folder's `AGENTS.md` or which skill loads for which kind of work. The code-layout, branch and bootstrap sections moved out to the folder-scoped files.

nodes.label: crates/AGENTS.md
nodes.subtitle: rules for crates/
nodes.summary: New folder-scoped rules: the thin-binary and one-crate-per-group layout, Rust as the engine language, and the four commands to run before pushing a change under `crates/`.

nodes.label: .github/workflows/AGENTS.md
nodes.subtitle: rules for workflow files
nodes.summary: New folder-scoped rules for workflow authors: define merge-deciding jobs on the base branch, never check out a pull request's code into a job holding a secret, pin actions to a commit SHA, scope permissions, and start secret-holding jobs with harden-runner in block mode.

nodes.label: .agents/skills/
nodes.subtitle: 7 repository-internal skills
nodes.summary: The new home for skills used only while working on this repository: adding-an-osf-command, filing-an-issue, opening-a-pull-request, reviewing-a-pull-request, running-sub-agents, writing-a-workflow, plus the folder README. Each skill states its rules and marks each one checked or not checked.

nodes.label: .claude/skills
nodes.subtitle: symlink to ../.agents/skills
nodes.summary: A git symlink, mode 120000, so Claude Code reads the same skill files as every other agent instead of a drifting copy. CI fails the build if it is not a real symlink or points somewhere else.

nodes.label: skills/
nodes.subtitle: skills shipped to adopters
nodes.summary: The skills this repository ships, `show-me` and `pr-outline`. The new README states the split: a skill only this repository uses lives in `.agents/skills/`, a skill it also ships keeps its one source here.

nodes.label: scan.rs tests
nodes.subtitle: 5 new symlink cases
nodes.summary: New integration tests covering a tracked symlink to a directory, a repository whose only entry is a link, an explicit symlinked directory path, a link found while walking a folder, and a link that cycles back on an ancestor. `TempRepo::symlink` was added to the shared test helper.

edges.label: osf scan
edges.summary: The binary parses arguments and calls the scan entry point; all logic stays in the library.

edges.label: (targets, skipped)
edges.summary: The call now returns a skipped-link count alongside the targets, and that count seeds the excluded total.

edges.label: walk each given path
edges.summary: Each explicitly named path is walked, with the skipped counter threaded through the recursion.

edges.label: symlink_metadata
edges.summary: The walk now stats with `symlink_metadata` and stops at any symlink, incrementing the skipped count instead of descending. This is the change that makes a cyclic link terminate.

edges.label: no paths given
edges.summary: With no paths, the scan set is git's tracked files and the skipped count is zero.

edges.label: counted as excluded
edges.summary: Before reading a resolved target, `scan_paths` re-checks it with `symlink_metadata`; a link is counted as excluded and never read. This catches tracked links, which arrive through the git path rather than the walk.

edges.label: read bytes
edges.summary: Non-link targets are read from disk, skipped if binary, and handed to the rule engine.

edges.label: Rules + Excluder
edges.summary: The excluder filters by label before any read; the rules judge the files that survive.

edges.label: hygiene job
edges.summary: The hygiene job runs `osf scan` over tracked files and over each commit message a pull request adds.

edges.label: osf lint skill
edges.summary: A new step collects every `skills/*/SKILL.md` and `.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md` directory and lints them all on every run.

edges.label: mode must be 120000
edges.summary: A new step reads the git mode of `.claude/skills` and its link target, failing the build with a fix hint if either is wrong.

edges.label: ../.agents/skills
edges.summary: The symlink resolves to the shared skills folder, so Claude Code and every other agent read one set of files.

edges.label: working under crates/
edges.summary: The root file's routing table sends a reader working under `crates/` to the folder-scoped rules.

edges.label: working under .github/workflows/
edges.summary: The same table routes workflow work to the workflow rules.

edges.label: task-matched skills
edges.summary: The table names each skill and the moment it loads, so a rule tied to one moment reaches the agent only when the task matches.

edges.label: 5 symlink cases
edges.summary: The new tests drive `scan_paths` directly and through the binary, asserting that links are never read and always counted.

flows.title: A scan that meets a symlink
flows.summary: What happens when `osf scan` is pointed at a folder containing a link, or at a repository whose tracked entries include one. The link is counted as excluded at whichever stage sees it first, and never read.

messages.label: resolve targets
messages.note: Now returns a skipped-link count alongside the labelled targets.

messages.label: symlink_metadata
messages.note: A link is counted in `skipped` and the walk returns without descending, so a link cycling back on an ancestor terminates.

messages.label: (targets, skipped)
messages.note: `skipped` seeds `dropped`, so the excluded total already includes links found during the walk.

messages.label: symlink_metadata per target
messages.note: Catches tracked links, which arrive through the git path and never pass through the walk.

messages.label: read bytes, apply rules
messages.note: Only non-link, non-binary, non-excluded files reach the rules.

messages.label: ScanOutcome { files, excluded }
messages.note: A scan of nothing but links now reports a non-zero excluded count instead of reading as clean.
